info.title: CityFix API
info.description:
CityFix — citizen-powered city issue reporting & tracking.

## Authentication

Authentication is a signed, HTTP-only session cookie named `cityfix_session`.
Sign in through one of the auth endpoints below; the response sets the cookie
and every subsequent request must carry it.

The cookie value is `<sessionId>.<hmac-sha256-hex>` — opaque to clients,
tamper-evident server-side. Attributes: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`,
`Path=/`, `Secure` in production. The session expires 14 days after it is
issued (the expiry is fixed, not sliding).

### Roles

Four roles: `citizen`, `dispatcher`, `crew`, `admin`.

- **citizen** — files and tracks their own reports.
- **dispatcher** — triages the ward queue, assigns crews, transitions tickets.
- **crew** — works the tickets assigned to them and uploads after-photos.
- **admin** — city-wide configuration. Admin **writes** additionally require a
  fresh WebAuthn assertion (ADR-007): a password login lets an admin *read*
  the admin surfaces but not change them.

## Scope enforcement

Dispatcher and crew sessions are bound to a `(city, ward, department)` scope.
A request for a ticket outside that scope is refused.

## Rate limiting

A per-key token bucket allows roughly one request per second, with a burst
capacity of 1 in production and 4 in development. Exceeding it returns 429
with a `Retry-After` header.

## Known inconsistencies

This API is not internally uniform, and the spec documents the current
behaviour rather than a normalised ideal:

- The unauthenticated error code is `not_authenticated` on most routes, but
  `unauthenticated` under `/api/v1/admin/**` and on `/api/profile`.
- Query-parameter validation failures return `invalid_query` on the
  dispatcher and crew list routes, but `invalid_input` elsewhere.
- The rate-limit retry field is `retryAfterMs` on most routes, but
  `retry_after_ms` on `GET /api/tickets/{id}`.
- An illegal transition returns 409 `invalid_transition` on
  `POST /api/tickets/{id}/transition`, but 422 `illegal_transition` on the
  v1 dispatcher and crew transition routes.

## Excluded

The `/api/dev/**` routes are development-only tooling and are deliberately
not documented here.

post.description: The step-up ceremony for an admin who is ALREADY signed in. Unlike `/api/auth/webauthn/assertion` (which mints a session and is the login flow), this route mints nothing: it verifies possession of the authenticator and refreshes the challenge ledger row that the `requireWebAuthn` guard reads, so the admin’s next gated write succeeds. The challenge is always bound to the session’s own user — a challenge issued for another user is rejected with 403.

get.description: Returns every report the citizen filed in their city, newest first. There is no pagination — the route accepts no query parameters.

403.description: Only citizens have a personal report list.

post.description:
Creates a report in the citizen’s city and files it under the given ward and category.

A near-duplicate is **not** merged. When another open report sits within the
city’s dedup radius this returns 200 with a `dedup_match` prompt and creates
nothing; the citizen can then re-POST with `dedupDeclineTicketId` to file it
anyway, which raises a review flag for the dispatcher.

Two reports filed at the *identical* location at the same instant are also
de-duplicated, by the database rather than by the scan: a unique index on the
location key refuses the second insert and the loser is returned the same
`dedup_match` prompt. A report filed after a `dedupDeclineTicketId` is exempt
from that index — an acknowledged duplicate must always be creatable.

photoBlobs.description: Raw photo bytes, base64-encoded, for upload to the blob store.

dedupDeclineTicketId.description: The ticket id of the dedup match the citizen chose to file alongside.

200.description: A possible duplicate was found — nothing was created. The citizen can decline the match and re-POST.

400.description: Validation failed, or the ward/category belongs to another city.

403.description: The report was filed against a different city than the session.

409.description: A concurrent submission of the same location won the dedup race, and the winning ticket could not be resolved afterwards. The citizen should retry.

413.description: A photo exceeded the size limit.

500.description: The report was created but could not be read back.

post.description:
The legacy staff transition route. Preferred over the v1 dispatcher and crew
transition routes, which enforce a narrower per-role status allow-list.

Allowed transitions: `submitted → routed | cancelled`, `routed → in_progress |
cancelled`, `in_progress → resolved | cancelled`. `resolved`, `closed` and
`cancelled` are terminal.

get.description: Lists the crew that can be assigned in a ward, ordered by current load (least busy first), then by name. When `categoryId` is supplied the crew are filtered to that category’s department, plus any crew with no department (general-purpose responders). Each entry carries the crew member’s `activeCount` — the number of active (non-terminal) reports they hold — and `atCapacity`, so the dispatcher can see who is already carrying their share. The assignment endpoint is the load-bearing check; this list is a hint.

post.summary: Assign a crew member to a report
post.description: Assigns a crew member, or clears the assignment by sending `null`. The crew member must exist, be a crew role, and belong to the report’s ward and department — otherwise the assignment would be invisible to them. A crew member already holding the maximum number of active reports is refused with `409 crew_at_capacity`; the report being assigned is excluded from that count, so re-assigning a report the member already holds is never blocked by capacity.

409.description: Another writer changed the report first, or the crew member is already at capacity.

put.description:
Only the display names are writable, and only on the caller’s OWN row — the write is scoped to the session’s user, so one user can never edit another’s profile.

ADR-007: an ADMIN write is an admin write wherever it lives, so it requires a fresh WebAuthn assertion. A citizen / dispatcher / crew write to their own profile is NOT an admin write and is not gated. The body is validated BEFORE the ceremony (ADR-007 guard ordering), so a malformed request gets a 400 rather than being sent through a hardware-key prompt it could never satisfy.

deltaPercent.description: Percentage change vs the immediately-preceding window of the same length.

durationMs.description: Raw milliseconds — only on the duration stat.

value.description: 0..100 for the percentage signals; milliseconds for the duration signal.

comparison.description: The Dhaka overlay. Null unless `compare=1` and the Dhaka city exists.

RateLimited.description: Rate limited. The `Retry-After` header carries the wait in seconds.

retryAfterMs.description: Milliseconds until the next request is allowed.

Forbidden.description: The session does not have the required role or scope.
